recommendation: Keep the fixed commit. It completes the accepted Range/RatioRange modeling change in current build-scope source without restoring obsolete high-limit elements or changing unrelated Ingredient strength examples.
issue_request: FHIR-31821 was Published/Persuasive for BRR MedicinalProductIngredient and asked why strength ranges were modeled with high/low ratio-style fields rather than Range plus an explicit base quantity; the accepted resolution was to add a choice of Range and RatioRange.
initial_application: Upstream commits aa11acd4e322ff53f1d98f256f0f975871947ee2 and a9e29cf42c14a7214228b49ed2aa225d436ede9e removed presentationHighLimit, concentrationHighLimit, and referenceStrength.strengthHighLimit from Ingredient and added RatioRange to the corresponding choice elements, but they did not add Range.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini marks Ingredient as active and maps the old MedicinalProductIngredient artifact to Ingredient. FHIR-19416 introduced RatioRange for ratio ranges and cited medicinal product ingredient strength as a motivating use case. Later RatioRange choice-type discussion and FHIR-34453 support the existing RatioRange use but do not supersede the Range part of FHIR-31821.
reconciliation: Added Range to Ingredient.substance.strength.presentation[x], Ingredient.substance.strength.concentration[x], and Ingredient.substance.strength.referenceStrength.strength[x] in source/ingredient/structuredefinition-Ingredient.xml, and aligned source/ingredient/ingredient.svg so the checked resource diagram shows the same choice list.
source_changes: source/ingredient/structuredefinition-Ingredient.xml: added Range as an allowed choice type on Ingredient.substance.strength.presentation[x], Ingredient.substance.strength.concentration[x], and Ingredient.substance.strength.referenceStrength.strength[x].
source/ingredient/ingredient.svg: aligned the checked Ingredient UML diagram with the updated Range choice entries from the authoritative StructureDefinition source.

related_jiras.note: Introduced RatioRange for ranges of ratios and named medicinal product ingredient strength as a use case.
Later clarified RatioRange's use as an explicit choice type; it supports the existing RatioRange context but does not remove FHIR-31821's Range requirement.
